title: Grateful Dead Live at Carousel Ballroom on 1968-03-29
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Stunning matrix recording captures a swinging 1968 show highlighted by an epic New Potato Caboose and crystal‑clear Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The March 29, 1968 Carousel Ballroom performance is praised for its high‑energy swing and standout moments such as New Potato Caboose, Dark Star and Death Don't Have No Mercy. Charlie Miller’s matrix transfer delivers an open, crisp sound that lets the instruments breathe while still letting crowd chatter seep through, giving listeners a vivid sense of being there. Overall the musical execution is considered one of the best early‑68 shows despite a few missing tracks.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of detailed reviews award 5 stars and highlight both superb performance and excellent sound quality; the average rating across all reviews is ~4.2, supporting a strong positive score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early band‑created soundboard/stage‑mic matrix with crystal‑clear instrument separation; occasional hall echo and crowd chatter audible but adds atmosphere. No major dropouts or distortion reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set swings like early‑68 shows, with a lively first half and an expansive second half; an announcer appears after Morning Dew suggesting a brief break. Transitions are praised and the overall pacing feels natural despite some crowd noise.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s solos on New Potato Caboose and Dark Star are described as sublime, top‑tier guitar work that borders on legendary.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocal solo is noted, with a humorous mention of Pigpen cursing his organ during it.
